text: Two points \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on line \(y=2x+3\). These two points \(P\) and \(Q\) are at a distance of 2 units from another point \(R(1,5)\). What are the coordinates of \(P\) and \(Q\)?
solution:
Let \(P=(a,2a+3)\), a point of the line \(y = 2x + 3\). Then \(PR^2=(a-1)^2+(2a-2)^2=5(a-1)^2\).

\(PR = 2\) gives \(5(a-1)^2=4\), so \(a = 1 \pm \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\) and \(2a + 3 = 5 \pm \frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\).

So \(P\) and \(Q\) are \(\left(1+\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}},5+\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\) and \(\left(1-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}},5-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\). Hence (A).

label: NDA 2025-I Q54 (Lines)
reason: fix: NDA 2025-I Q54 (scanned paper, page 17): prints 'at a distance sqrt2 units from P'; our copy had 2 and key (c). With sqrt2, Q = (3, 1) or (1, -1): answer (b), as the transcribed key.
text: Let \(A(3,-1)\) and \(B(1,1)\) be the end points of line segment AB. Let P be the middle point of the line segment AB. Let Q be the point situated at a distance \(\sqrt{2}\) units from P on the perpendicular bisector line of AB. What are the possible coordinates of Q?
solution:
Midpoint \(P = (2, 0)\). Slope of \(AB = \frac{1-(-1)}{1-3} = -1\), so the perpendicular bisector has slope 1: \(y = x - 2\).

Let \(Q = (x, x - 2)\). \(PQ = \sqrt{2}\) gives \((x-2)^2 + (x-2)^2 = 2\), so \((x-2)^2 = 1\) and \(x = 3\) or \(x = 1\).

So \(Q = (3, 1)\) or \((1, -1)\); of these only \((3, 1)\) is offered. Hence (B).

text: If \(2x^2 + 2y^2 + 4x + 5y + 1 = 0\) and \(3x^2 + 3y^2 + 6x - 7y + 3k = 0\) are orthogonal, then value of \(k\) is
solution:
Normalize: Circle 1 \(x^2 + y^2 + 2x + \tfrac{5}{2}y + \tfrac{1}{2} = 0\), so \(g_1 = 1, f_1 = \tfrac{5}{4}, c_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}\). Circle 2 \(x^2 + y^2 + 2x - \tfrac{7}{3}y + k = 0\), so \(g_2 = 1, f_2 = -\tfrac{7}{6}, c_2 = k\).

Orthogonality: \(2(g_1 g_2 + f_1 f_2) = c_1 + c_2 \Rightarrow 2\left(1 - \tfrac{35}{24}\right) = \tfrac{1}{2} + k\), that is \(-\tfrac{11}{12} = \tfrac{1}{2} + k\). So \(k = -\tfrac{17}{12}\). Hence (D).

reason: note: Oswaal NDA sample paper 1 Q67 (source PDF not on disk): two opposite vertices do not fix a rectangle; key (c) is the axis-parallel reading.
solution:
**Note:** Two opposite vertices do not fix a rectangle: its area can be anything up to half the square of the diagonal. The answer shown takes the sides parallel to the axes, the reading the options intend.

With the sides parallel to the coordinate axes, the other two vertices are \((5, -2)\) and \((-3, 7)\).

One side runs horizontally and has length \(\left|5 - (-3)\right| = 8\).

The adjacent side runs vertically and has length \(\left|7 - (-2)\right| = 9\).

Area \(= 8 \times 9 = 72\) sq. units. Hence (C).
